cues.en: or sitting in an adjacent room where the same lecture was broadcast via closed circuit TV.

cues.en: What would you prefer?

cues.en: In the 80s there was no debating.

cues.zh: 计算机是解决教育困境的革命性方案。
cues.en: Computers were the revolutionary solution to our education woes.

cues.zh: 它们视听结合、可交互，还能编程实现几乎任何你想要的功能。
cues.en: They were audiovisual, interactive, and could be programmed to do almost anything you like.

cues.en: Well at the time, they could run Oregon Trail.

cues.en: But their potential was obvious.

cues.en: Researches suspected that if they could teach kids to program, say how to move a turtle

cues.zh: 在屏幕上移动，那么他们的程序性推理能力也会提高。
cues.en: around a screen, then their procedural reasoning skills would also improve.

cues.en: So how did it go?

cues.zh: 并未受到影响。
cues.en: unaffected.

cues.en: quote, “The use of videodiscs in classroom instruction is increasing every year and promises

cues.en: to revolutionize what will happen in the classroom of tomorrow.”

cues.zh: 影碟？
cues.en: Videodiscs?

cues.en: Yeah, those giant oversized CD things.

cues.en: Remember when they revolutionized education?

cues.zh: 如今，许多东西都有望彻底改变教育，比如智能白板、智能手机、
cues.en: Nowadays plenty of things are poised to revolutionize education like, smartboards, smartphones,

cues.en: tables, and M.O.O.C.s.

cues.en: And some belief we’re getting close to universal teaching machine, a computer so quick and

cues.en: well-programmed that it’s basically like having your own personal tutor in a machine.

cues.zh: 学生可以按照自己的节奏学习结构良好的课程，获得即时
cues.en: A student could work through well-structured lessons at their own pace receiving immediate

cues.en: and personally-tailored feedback, and all without the interference of a meddlesome and

cues.zh: 昂贵的老师来干涉。
cues.en: expensive teacher.

cues.zh: 这些说法听起来耳熟吗？
cues.en: Do these claims sound familiar?

cues.zh: 过去100年里，生活的许多领域都发生了彻底变革，但教育
cues.en: Over the past 100 years, a lot of areas of life have been revolutionized, but education

cues.zh: 并不在其中。
cues.en: is not one of them.

cues.zh: 总的来说，学生们仍然是由一位老师分组教学。
cues.en: By in large, students are still taught in groups by a single teacher.

cues.zh: 而这并不是一场革命该有的样子。
cues.en: And that is not what a revolution looks like.

cues.zh: 有些人可能会把这种状况归咎于教育机构的惰性。
cues.en: Some might blame this state of affairs on the inertia of our educational institutions.

cues.zh: 要让庞大的官僚体系做出改变，实在太难了。
cues.en: It’s just too hard to get a huge bureaucracy to change.

cues.zh: 但我认为，技术之所以未能革新教育，原因在别处，
cues.en: But I think the reason technology hasn’t revolutionized education is something else,

cues.zh: 这个原因直指教育的本质。
cues.en: something that goes to the very heart of what education is.

cues.zh: 让我们来思考一下学习的过程。
cues.en: Let’s consider the process of learning.

cues.zh: 假设你想教别人人类心脏是如何泵血的。
cues.en: Say you want to teach someone how a human heart pumps blood.

cues.zh: 你觉得哪种学习辅助手段更有效，是这段带解说的动画，还是
cues.en: Which learning aid do you think would be more effective, this animation with narration or

cues.zh: 这套配文字的静态图片？
cues.en: this set of static picture with text?

cues.zh: 显然动画更好。
cues.en: Obviously the animation is better.

cues.zh: 我的意思是，至少它精确展示了心脏在做什么。
cues.en: I mean for one thing it shows exactly what the heart does.

cues.zh: 几十年来，教育研究一直聚焦于这类问题。
cues.en: For decades, educational research focused on questions like this.

cues.zh: 视频比书籍更能促进学习吗？
cues.en: Does a video promote learning better than a book?

cues.zh: 现场讲座比电视讲座更有效吗？
cues.en: Are live lectures more effective than televised lectures?

cues.zh: 动画比静态图形更好吗？
cues.en: Is animation better than static graphics?

cues.zh: 在所有控制良好的研究中，结果都是没有显著差异。
cues.en: In all well-controlled studies, the result is no significant difference.

cues.zh: 也就是说，只要两种处理方式的内容是等价的，学习效果
cues.en: That is, so long as the content is equivalent between the two treatments, the learning outcomes

cues.zh: 在所有不同媒介上都是相同的。
cues.en: are the same with all different media.

cues.zh: 这怎么可能？
cues.en: How is this possible?

cues.zh: 像动画这样看似强大的东西，怎么会并不比
cues.en: How can something which seems so powerful, like animation, be no more effective than

cues.zh: 静态图形更有效呢？
cues.en: static graphics?

cues.zh: 首先，动画转瞬即逝，所以你可能会错过一些东西
cues.en: Well for one thing, animations are fleeting and so you might miss something as they go
by.

cues.zh: 另外，既然各个部分是为你动态呈现的，你就不必在脑中想象
cues.en: Plus, since the parts are animated for you, you don’t have to mentally envision how

cues.zh: 这些部分是如何运动的。
cues.en: the parts are moving.

cues.zh: 这样你就不用投入太多脑力，反而更容易记住。
cues.en: And so you don’t have to invest as much mental effort which would make it more memorable.

cues.zh: 事实上，有时候静态图形比动画效果更好。
cues.en: In fact, sometimes static graphics perform better than animations.

cues.zh: 我认为这指向了教育中一个非常根本的方面，那就是
cues.en: And I think this points to a really fundamental aspect of education which is, it doesn’t

cues.zh: 学习者周围发生了什么并不重要。
cues.en: matter what happens around the learner.

cues.zh: 我们能给学生提供的体验并不受限。
cues.en: We are not limited by the experiences we can give to students.

cues.zh: 真正限制学习的是学生头脑内部能发生什么。
cues.en: What limits learning is what can happen inside the student’s head.

cues.zh: 学习的核心部分正是在那里发生的。
cues.en: That is where the important part of learning takes place.

cues.zh: 没有哪种技术天生就优于其他技术。
cues.en: No technology is inherently superior to any other.

cues.zh: 研究人员花了大量时间研究某种媒介或技术是否比另一种
cues.en: Researchers spent so much time investigating whether one medium or technology was more

cues.zh: 更有效，却没能去研究究竟该如何使用技术
cues.en: effective than another that they failed to investigate exactly how to use the technology

cues.zh: 来促进有意义的思维过程。
cues.en: to promote meaningful thought processes.

cues.zh: 那么真正的问题就是，什么样的体验能促进学习所需的那种思维
cues.en: So the question really is what experiences promote the kind of thinking that is required

cues.zh: 呢？
cues.en: for learning?

cues.zh: 最近，这方面的研究正在进行，我们发现了一些相当重要的
cues.en: Recently, that research is being conducted and we’re finding out some pretty important

cues.zh: 东西。
cues.en: stuff.

cues.zh: 我的意思是，这也许看起来显而易见，但事实证明，把词语和图像结合起来学习，
cues.en: I mean it may seem obvious, but it turns out learning with words and pictures together,

cues.zh: 无论是动画加旁白，还是静态图片加文字，效果都更好
cues.en: whether they’re animation and narration or static pictures and text, works better

cues.zh: 比只用词语要好。
cues.en: than words alone.

cues.zh: 另外，我们发现，任何多余的东西都需要从课程中剔除。
cues.en: Also, we see that anything which is extraneous needs to be eliminated from a lesson.

cues.zh: 例如，屏幕上的文字会与视觉画面争夺注意力，所以学习者在
cues.en: For example, on-screen text competes with visuals, so learners perform better when it

cues.zh: 没有文字时比有文字时表现更好。
cues.en: is omitted than when it is present.

cues.zh: 既然我们知道了如何最好地制作教育视频，而且任何体验都可以在
cues.en: Now that we know how best to make educational videos, and any experience can be simulated

cues.zh: 视频环境中模拟，那么YouTube必定是那个将彻底改变教育的平台。
cues.en: in the video setting, YouTube must be the platform that will revolutionize education.

cues.zh: 我是说，YouTube上的教育视频每天都在增加。
cues.en: I mean the number of educational videos on YouTube is increasing every day.

cues.zh: 那我们为什么还需要老师？
cues.en: So why do we need teachers?

cues.zh: 好吧，如果你认为老师的根本工作是把信息
cues.en: Well, if you think that the fundamental job of a teacher is to transmit information from

cues.zh: 从他们脑袋里传递到学生脑袋里，那你说得对，老师确实过时了。
cues.en: their head to their students’, then you’re right, they are obsolete.

cues.zh: 我是说，你大概会想象这样一个课堂：老师滔滔不绝地讲事实，语速
cues.en: I mean, you probably imagine a classroom where this teacher is spewing out facts at a pace

cues.zh: 对一个学生合适，对一半人太快，对其余的人又太慢。
cues.en: which is appropriate for one student, too fast for half, and too slow for the rest.

cues.zh: 幸运的是，老师的根本角色并不是传递信息。
cues.en: Luckily the fundamental role of a teachers is not to deliver information.

cues.zh: 而是引导学习的社会过程。
cues.en: It is to guide the social process of learning.

cues.zh: 老师的工作是启发、挑战、激发学生，让他们想要学习。
cues.en: The job of a teacher is to inspire, to challenge, to excite their students to want to learn.

cues.zh: 是的，他们也会讲解、演示、展示东西，但从根本上说，那
cues.en: Yes, they also do explain and demonstrate and show things, but fundamentally that is

cues.zh: 并不是重点。
cues.en: beside the point.

cues.zh: 老师最重要的事，是让每个学生都感到自己很重要，
cues.en: The most important thing a teacher does is make every student feel like they are important,

cues.zh: 让他们感到要对自己的学习负责。
cues.en: to make them feel accountable for doing the work of learning.

cues.zh: 这一切并不是说技术对教育没有影响。
cues.en: All of this is not to say technology has had no impact on education.

cues.zh: 学生和老师通过电脑工作和交流。
cues.en: Students and teachers work and communicate via computers.

cues.zh: 视频在课堂内外都有使用。
cues.en: And videos are used both inside and outside of classrooms.

cues.zh: 但这一切最好被描述为一种演进，而不是革命。
cues.en: But all of this is best characterized as an evolution, not a revolution.

cues.zh: 教育的基础仍然建立在老师与学生之间的社会互动之上，
cues.en: The foundation of education is still based on the social interaction between teachers

cues.zh: 以及学生之间。
cues.en: and students.

cues.zh: 尽管每一项新技术看起来都颇具变革性，比如电影、电脑
cues.en: For as transformative as each new technology seems to be, like motion pictures or computer

cues.zh: 或智能白板，真正重要的是学习者头脑内部发生的事。
cues.en: or smartboards, what really matters is what happens inside the learner’s head.

cues.zh: 而让学习者思考，似乎最好是在与其他学习者
cues.en: And making a learner think seems best achieved in a social environment with other learners

cues.zh: 和一位有爱心的老师的社会环境中实现。
cues.en: and a caring teacher.
